name: Canada
sources: GDP $596bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series CAN, 1990 - the print is $596,075,591,361, and it is the same series this roster's USA 5980, France 1270, Italy 1180 and UK 1090 sit on, which is the reason it is the figure entered rather than a national-accounts one. The cross-check, stated rather than hidden: Statistics Canada put GDP at market prices near C$680bn in 1990, and at the year's average market rate of about 1.167 CAD/USD that is roughly $583bn. The 2% gap is Atlas smoothing in the World Bank series, not a disagreement about Canadian output.

Population 27.7m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series CAN, 1990 = 27,691,138. The 1991 census of 4 June counted 27,296,859 on a de jure basis; the World Bank figure is the mid-year estimate and is the one used, again for comparability with the rest of the roster.

Inflation 4.8%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, series CAN, 1990 = 4.78%. The GST was legislated in 1990 and took effect on 1 January 1991, so its one-off price-level effect falls outside this figure and inside the first game year - which is the correct place for it, because the model should discover that tax rise rather than be told about it.

Interest rate 13.0%: the Bank of Canada bank rate, which ran between about 12.4% and its peak of 14.05% in May 1990 and averaged near 13%. This is the widest real-rate gap of any democracy in the roster and it is not a typo: John Crow had announced a zero-inflation target in January 1988 and was defending a dollar that reached US$0.89, holding Canadian rates four to five points above American ones through a recession that began in the second quarter of 1990. The coupled constraint the schema imposes is comfortable at 0.025 - (0.130 - 0.048) = -0.057.

TFP trend 0.008: Canadian multifactor productivity growth was already weak through the 1980s and got weaker - the gap in output per hour against the United States widened for most of the following decade, and the productivity puzzle is still the central question in Canadian economics. Entered below Australia's 0.011, because Australia's microeconomic reform programme was in progress and Canada's was substantially the free trade agreement alone, and above New Zealand's 0.007. Noted for the next person, because the schema is easy to misread: tech/mod.rs rewrites this field every tick, so it seeds the technology state rather than setting the growth path, and moving it is not how the growth calibration gets tuned.

Revenue 43% of GDP: total general-government revenue on the OECD basis - federal, ten provinces, municipalities and the Canada and Quebec Pension Plans together. Canada's federal share alone is under 20%, and entering that instead would have made the most heavily provincial state in the roster look like the least taxed, which is the specific way a federation gets transcribed wrong.

Gross public debt 73% of GDP: general-government gross financial liabilities, OECD basis, 1990. Federal net debt alone was near 55%. Entered above Spain's 0.43 and below Italy's 0.94, which is where Canada sat: the second-worst fiscal position in the G7 and the one Moody's would downgrade in 1994.

Military 2.0% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, series CAN, 1990 = 1.96%. Strength 12 is an index, not personnel: roughly 87,000 all-volunteer regulars, 4 Canadian Mechanized Brigade Group and 1 Canadian Air Division forward-based in Germany, three destroyer squadrons and no strategic lift. Indexed below Spain's 16 - Spain fielded three times the personnel - and well below Italy's 26, which is the honest ranking of a serious NATO contributor with no independent reach.

Investment 21.7% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, series CAN, 1990 = 21.70%. The split entered here, 3.0 public and 18.7 private, is an apportionment rather than a transcription: the World Bank series is total gross fixed capital formation and does not decompose by sector. Canadian general-government fixed investment ran near 3% of GDP in this period and the residual is assigned to the private sector so that the two sum to the published total. The total is sourced; the split is reasoned, and is said here to be reasoned.

Oil 1.7 mbd: Canadian crude oil production in 1990, per the Canada Energy Regulator's thirty-year review of crude exports, which takes 1.7 mbd as the 1990 base against which subsequent growth is measured. Totals including natural gas liquids and synthetic crude from the Athabasca upgraders run nearer 2.0 mbd; the crude figure is entered because that is what the schema's field asks for and what the UK's 1.9 alongside it means.

Separatism 0.38 and stability 64: this is the highest separatism figure of any democracy in the roster and 1990 is the reason. The Meech Lake Accord died on 23 June when Manitoba and Newfoundland failed to ratify; Lucien Bouchard left the cabinet in May and founded the Bloc Quebecois on 15 June; Quebec sovereignty support passed 60% in polling that summer and the Belanger-Campeau commission was struck in September. The Oka standoff ran from 11 July to 26 September with the army deployed against Mohawk barricades in a Montreal suburb. Set above Turkey's 0.30 - which is a shooting war, but a war over a region holding a fifth of the country - because Quebec is a quarter of Canada's people and voted 49.42% to leave five years later. Set well below Yugoslavia's 0.72, because the whole of the Canadian argument was conducted by referendum. Stability 64 records a constitutional crisis inside institutions nobody doubted, below Spain's 70 and far below Australia's 76.

Authoritarianism 0.08: a Westminster democracy with an entrenched Charter of Rights since 1982 and courts that strike down statute under it. Entered between Australia's 0.06 and New Zealand's 0.10, and the ordering of the three is argued rather than assumed. Australia is lowest: a written constitution, High Court judicial review, federalism, and an elected Senate that genuinely blocks. Canada has all of that except the blocking upper house, and has section 33 - the notwithstanding clause, used by Quebec in 1988 to override the Supreme Court on commercial signage. A legislature that can vote itself out of a rights guarantee is not the same object as one that cannot. New Zealand is highest for the reasons set out in its own file.

pop_growth_1990 = 1.2714%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series CAN (Canada): 25,607,053 in 1984 to 27,276,781 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 15 were held and are listed below with their citations; 33 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, comp_risc_superscalar, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. core_packet_internetworking -> NOT HELD (semiconductors-computing said held, telecom-space said not held; resolved to the board that owns the Communications domain, telecom-space).

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 6 cells: bio_cross_sectional_imaging (health and agriculture board), bio_monoclonal_antibody (health and agriculture board), bio_recombinant_pharma (health and agriculture board), core_pcr (health and agriculture board), ener_horizontal_drilling (energy and transport board), tran_electronic_freight_documents (energy and transport board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Krawetz SA, Pon RT, Dixon GH, 'Increased efficiency of the Taq polymerase catalyzed polymerase chain reaction', Nucleic Acids Research 1989;17(2):819 (PMID 2915939), Department of Medical Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, University of Calgary. January 1989, and again a method-improvement paper on Taq-catalysed PCR rather than a first use. Corroborated in the same window by the Laboratory Centre for Disease Control, Health Protection Branch, Tunney's Pasture, Ottawa, developing a PCR protocol for Chlamydia detection (PMID 2615767) - a national public-health laboratory, which is the service end of the claim. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 10.53 PCs per 100, 4.3x the World value of 2.45.

Oracle established a Canadian subsidiary within three years of 1982 (Oracle corporate histories, as above); Canada is also named among the five locations of Oracle's 17 international marketing subsidiaries as at 1986. Canada also holds comp_microprocessor at 10.53 PCs per 100.

R3: Cantel and Bell Cellular both launched Canadian cellular service on 1 July 1985, the first call being placed from Nathan Phillips Square, Toronto, to Montreal. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 583,766 Canadian mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990. Northern Telecom's DMS-100 digital exchange was a Canadian product in domestic service.

Anik D1 was launched on 26 August 1982 with Spar Aerospace Limited of Toronto as prime contractor - the first Canadian prime contractor for a spacecraft - handling the full satellite bus design including propulsion, power and attitude control for geostationary operation, for Telesat Canada. Spar was prime for the whole Anik D series, 1982-1984.

Cantel and Bell Cellular launched Canadian cellular service on 1 July 1985; the first call was made from Nathan Phillips Square, Toronto, to the mayor of Montreal. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 583,766 Canadian mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

LIMB A FAILS and is not used; granted on the named-artefact bar, same predicate as the Italy and France cells. LIMB B: Canada is in the Advanced Set. EVIDENCE E2, dated national firsts and a named facility: SASKATCHEWAN'S FIRST HORIZONTAL WELL WAS DRILLED IN 1987, with the Saskatchewan Research Council playing a key role in developing it (Saskatchewan Research Council, 'Drilling Through Advancements in Oil Production'). In Alberta in the same year, the Alberta Oil Sands Technology and Research Authority's UNDERGROUND TEST FACILITY - vertical mine shafts and horizontal tunnels from which horizontal wells were installed inside the oil sands deposit, and the facility on which steam-assisted gravity drainage was developed - was officially opened on 29 JUNE 1987. Canadian horizontal drilling then scaled immediately and heavily: about 750 horizontal wells were drilled in Canada from 1988 to 1992, and almost 45% of the Canadian horizontal wells drilled to that point were in the heavy oil fields of Saskatchewan and Alberta; Saskatchewan went from one well in 1987 to more than 500 drilled in 1997 alone. LIMB C SEARCHED: no named, citable fact was found placing Canada outside horizontal drilling before 1990. DISCLOSED LIMIT: the 750-well figure spans 1988-1992 and therefore straddles the start date, so it cannot tell us how many Canadian horizontal wells existed on 1 January 1990; it is quoted only as corroboration that the 1987 firsts were the start of an industry rather than isolated experiments. The grant rests on the two dated 1987 facts, both of which are unambiguously before the start date.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E4 - a binding national marketing authorisation in force in Canada six years before the board, which makes this the strongest cell in this technology. HUMULIN R / HUMULIN N / HUMULIN 30/70, 'insulin human injection, human biosynthetic, rDNA origin', Eli Lilly Canada Inc., Toronto: 'Date of Initial Approval: December 31, 1983', stated on the face of the Health Canada-filed product monograph (Health Canada Drug Product Database monograph document 00060544, https://pdf.hres.ca/dpd_pm/00060544.PDF, Submission Control 245812, ATC A10AB01/A10AC01/A10AD01). A named recombinant protein drug, a named marketing authorisation holder, the national regulator's own document, and a date. LIMB C SEARCHED AND CLEARED, WITH LIMB A VISIBLE IN CANADA'S OWN LITERATURE: the same regulator ended Canada's pituitary growth-hormone supply in 1985, reviewed in 'Growth hormone therapy in Canada: end of one era and beginning of another', Canadian Medical Association Journal 1986 (PMID 3089574). NOTE ON WHY THIS CELL IS INSULIN AND NOT hGH: a PubMed affiliation search for Canadian recombinant/biosynthetic/methionyl growth hormone clinical papers 1986-1990 returned nothing, so rather than infer Canadian hGH practice from the American pattern I moved to the authorisation, which is better evidence anyway.
WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, Canada, 1990: 88%. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('Canada,CAN,1990,88').

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E1/E2, from the national diffusion history: OTA, 'Health Care Technology and Its Assessment in Eight Countries' (OTA-BP-H-140, February 1995), chapter 3 'Health Care Technology in Canada (with special reference to Quebec)'. CT: 'The first CT scanner was installed in Canada in 1973 at the Montreal Neurological Institute'; in Ontario, after the province revised its target to one scanner per 300,000 persons in 1981, 'By 1986, 42 scanners were operating, and funding for an additional five had been approved'; and the Quebec series (chapter table 3-7, sourced to Gouvernement du Quebec, Ministere de la Sante et des Services sociaux, 'L'imagerie medicale au Quebec', 1986) records 35 scanning facilities in 1987 and an estimated 44 in 1989, against 3 in 1977. MRI: 'MRI was initially introduced in Canada as a research tool in 1982/83 ... The first clinical uses of MRI began in 1985', after which units reached all but two provinces. LIMB C SEARCHED AND CLEARED IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION: Canadian provincial governments repeatedly tried to RESTRAIN CT diffusion, and the OTA chapter describes Ontario's record as 'a cycle of reactive, ineffective policymaking by governments punctuated by continued efforts by hospitals to circumvent policies perceived to be limiting acquisition or diffusion of CT scanners' - the restraint failed, which is evidence of deployment rather than a defeater against it. Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half.

NAMED-ARTEFACT BAR, CLASS E2, two named Canadian institutions and two indications: Cardella CJ, Blake P, Cattran D, Cole E, 'Prophylactic OKT3 in renal retransplantation', Transplantation Proceedings 1989;21(2):3373-4 (PMID 2496509), Division of Nephrology, University of Toronto - prophylaxis, i.e. protocol use; and Weinshenker BG, Bass B, Ebers GC, Rice GP, 'Remission of psoriatic lesions with muromonab-CD3 (Orthoclone OKT3) treatment', Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology 1989;20(6):1132-3 (PMID 2502568), University Hospital, London, Ontario - therapeutic muromonab-CD3 administered OUTSIDE transplantation, which is only possible where the drug is on the hospital formulary. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.

CN loaded the first double-stack trains at Vancouver wharf for Toronto in February 1989, running weekly with Neptune Orient Lines and OOCL 5-Pak well cars, after testing a five-pak double-stack platform on CN train No 220 through western Canada on 28 November 1987; CN advertised the service with an inaugural five-pack Vancouver-Toronto run in May 1989. Trackside Treasure, 'CN Lasers, Five-Paks and Double-Stacks' (Sept 2019). NOTE: Canadian Pacific, the other transcontinental, did not begin double-stack until May 1991 after two years of testing, so the Canadian grant rests on CN alone.

LIMB A: UN/EDIFACT approved as ISO 9735 in 1987, and national electronic customs declaration systems in OECD public service before the start date, the board's own seven existing grants being the demonstration (see this node's note). LIMB B: Canada is in the Advanced Set. EVIDENCE E2 with an E1-flavoured penetration obligation attached: CADEX, the Customs Automated Data Exchange, is the Canadian system by which importers and brokers transmit their B3 accounting documents to Canadian customs electronically and receive processing acknowledgements and release decisions back. The CADEX System Project was established in November 1985 with an initial implementation date of 1 JANUARY 1988, and its design was worked out in consultation with the importing and brokerage community as a cost-reduction initiative aimed at eliminating the roughly four million dollars a year the department spent keying data into the Customs Commercial System. The programme carried published capture objectives: 20% of national B3 volumes in fiscal year 1988/89, 40% in fiscal 1989/90 and 60% in 1990/91. That last figure matters - it means CADEX was not merely switched on before the start date but was contracted to be carrying, and on its own targets was carrying, a measured double-digit national share of Canadian customs entries through 1989. Source: CADEX Participants' Requirements Document (Canada Border Services Agency, carrying the Revenue Canada Customs and Excise programme history); the 1988 introduction date is independently corroborated by a contemporaneous trade profile of a Toronto customs broker dating its adoption of Cadex to 1988. LIMB C SEARCHED: no named, citable fact was found placing Canada outside electronic customs filing before 1990. DISCLOSED LIMIT: CADEX carries the accounting document for goods that have already been released, not the release request itself; Canada's release-side system, ACROSS, is later. This is the same limb the existing USA cell rests on - ABI is an entry-filing interface - so the two cells are ruled to one standard rather than to two.

British Columbia salmon net-pen farming: the BC Salmon Farmers Association was formed in 1984, when there were 10 farms in the province; by 1988 about 118 active grow-out sites were producing 6,590 tonnes, and the provincial government had already imposed a moratorium on new farm approvals in 1986 and run the Gillespie inquiry - a regulatory response only an established industry provokes. Between 1989 and 1991, 26 companies, over 25% of the industry, went into receivership, which is a consolidation, not a start (BC government Salmon Aquaculture Review documents; BC salmon farming histories).
